title: 1905 c. John T G Carr's Store was built
description: John Thomas G. Carr, originally from England, arrived in Hartland in the mid to late 1800s. After apprenticing with a local retailer, he opened his own small store in 1884. In 1905, Carr further expanded his enterprise by constructing a modern three-storey brick commercial building, a symbol of solidity, purpose, and stability, which he named The Hartland Department Store. To make way for this impressive structure in the heart of the town’s business district, Carr moved his two-storey residence back across the rail tracks. The relocated house later served as the first home of the Dr. Walter Chestnut Library, located beside Craig’s Manufacturing on Orser Street.
